To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the main reasons for prescribing antibiotics were the fear of litigation and the fear of not being able to cure the patient.
the main reasons for the prescribing of antibiotics were fear, compliancy, insufficient knowledge and the external responsibility of patients, the pharmaceutical industry and over-the-counter drugs.

the factors/attitudes influencing inappropriate antibiotic prescribing by primary care physicians in Spain are fear, complacency and insufficient knowledge; the groups felt that antibiotic prescribing was not a problem in their community; and the factors/attitude that influence inappropriate antibiotic prescribing by GPs are fear, complainty, insufficient knowledge and the external responsibility of the industry, patients and the over-the-counter antibiotics.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of attitudes related to inappropriate antibiotic prescribing, with a view to designing interventions that target those shortcomings, with a view towards improving antibiotic use and helping to reduce the rate of resistance.
the identification of the attitudes/knowledge of primary care physicians related with inappropriate prescribing of antibiotics.

the identification of attitudes/knowledge associated with inappropriate antibiotic prescribing, which can be used to design interventions that specifically target these shortcomings in order to improve antibiotic use, and help reduce antibiotic resistance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are many factors which influence the prescription of antibiotics and that these factors vary between physicians, which makes the design of a single intervention difficult.

“the attitudes and opinions of the primary care physicians in our study are not consistent with the current guidelines for the use of antibiotics, nor do they reflect the current situation of antibiotic resistance in Spain.
there is an urgent need for the implementation of educational interventions to change the attitudes and behaviours of primary care physicians with respect to the prescribing of antibiotic drugs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in order for the problem to be solved, we need to improve our knowledge of the subject, and we must be more responsible in the way we prescribe antibiotics.
the use of antibiotics is a problem that is not only related to the physician, and that it is not only a problem for the patient, but also for society in general.
the physicians are aware of the importance of antibiotic resistance and they are concerned about it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for a change in the culture of prescribing in primary care.
the problem of antibiotic resistance is not perceived to exist in the community.
the FG method can be useful for identifying the attitudes of GPs towards antibiotic prescribing and resistance.
